en.html:
I was about to run across a small backstreet intersection when my feet stopped.

To my left, someone was walking away.

An ordinary man in ordinary town clothes. Nothing to stop for in that. But the walking itself was a little extraordinary.

Right, left, stumble. Full drunken swaying. On any other day I would have thought, achha, drunk, and left him to it.

Today, though, soldiers controlled the town. This was hardly the occasion for the public to take a pleasant tipsy zigzag through the streets.

So... what was going on with him?

While I was deciding whether to call out, something else came into view.

A car.

Not quite like the ones wealthy people of this age used to travel around town, or from one town to another. This sort did not normally come into town.

A military car. No roof, two foreign soldiers sitting inside.

...And this street was narrow. Put that big vehicle into it and a pedestrian would have to practically become part of the wall to let it pass.

Not such a difficult thing to do, surely.
But even that much seemed beyond our staggering gentleman.

He appeared to have noticed it coming straight toward him. Still he was moving slowly, as though his body would not do what he wanted. Drunk after all, was he?

At this rate the car would hit—

The driver looked absorbed. A child enjoying his game.
They wouldn't stop until they hit us at least once.

This time the car came very close to the wall. I waited until the last moment, jumped across, and barely got clear. That trick would not work next time.

The driver looked absorbed. A child enjoying his game.
They wouldn't stop until they hit us at least once.

They weren't trying to kill us.
Arre, their thoughts hadn't travelled that far.

Big heavy car hits person, person can easily die. Such advanced mathematics was beyond these two. First do it, then understand. Achha, like this somebody dies.
Then forget it straightaway.
Then do it again.

That foreign matter entering me—such deep disgust. I swayed, stumbling to keep my feet.

But that was all.

Now I felt fear. The three warriors surrounding me had not managed even a little of it.
This blind student had turned something far harsher than a wish for revenge upon me.

Not easy forgiveness. Nothing of that sort.

Protect the meaning, he said.
The meaning of Yuhi Nitta's death.

Which meant: carry that death forever.

...Haan. Of course. A heavy sentence, and entirely right. Right by the law of heaven itself.

Kill someone,
and for the rest of your life, that death is yours to carry.
